predictions.reasoning: A shift in the implied probability of AOC winning the 2028 Democratic nomination is a very long-horizon political signal with essentially no mechanistic link to any liquid asset over a 12-hour window. The 2028 election is years away, the nominee is undetermined, and even a sharp move in this single-candidate market carries little actionable macro information. Any market reaction would be dwarfed by ordinary intraday noise.

llm_justification.summary: This market asks about AOC winning the 2028 Democratic nomination — a distant, single-candidate political question. There is no credible mechanistic pathway from a shift in its implied probability to a meaningful move in any liquid public-market asset within a 12-hour window. Even a sharp anomaly here is more likely thin-market noise than leaked information affecting tradable assets. I map this as unclear with very low confidence and no tradable signal.
key_assumptions: The 2028 nomination remains undetermined and lacks near-term resolution catalysts
No concurrent breaking news that would independently move markets
Political nomination odds this far out do not systematically drive equity/FX/commodity prices intraday
failure_modes: A probability spike could coincide with a genuine market-moving news event (e.g., major policy proposal or health/legal news about a frontrunner) that this framing misattributes
Very thin liquidity makes the market prone to non-informative jumps
Even if a real progressive-policy narrative emerged, the proxy (SPY) is far too broad to capture it and any sector effect would be modest and slow
